mishnayos.summary: When a woman finds that she has become tamei, from when does her tumah start? Shammai, Hillel and the Sages each give a different answer about the pure things she touched before.

chunks.en: Shammai says,
for all women, their time is enough.
chunks.explain: Their tumah starts only from the moment they find it.

chunks.en: Hillel says,
from the last checking to this checking,
chunks.explain: She is tamei back to the last time she checked and was tahor.

chunks.en: and even if that was many days ago.
But the Sages say,

chunks.he: לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה,
chunks.en: not like this one and not like that one.
Rather, one full day back makes it shorter

words.note: From this time yesterday: a full day.

chunks.en: than the time from checking to checking,
and the time from checking to checking makes it shorter
than one full day back.
chunks.explain: She counts back whichever time is shorter.

chunks.en: Any woman who has a set time for this,
for her, her time is enough.
And a woman who checks with cloths
this counts like a checking,
and it makes shorter the full day back
and the time from checking to checking.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains what "her time is enough" means: if she finds she is tamei, only she is tamei, and the pure things she was handling stay tahor.

chunks.en: What does "her time is enough" mean?
She was sitting on the bed, busy with pure things,

words.note: Foods and things kept tahor.

chunks.en: and she stepped away and found she was tamei.
She is tamei, and all the pure things stay tahor.
Even though the Sages said
she makes things tamei for a full day back,
she counts only from the time that she found it.
chunks.explain: For counting her days, she starts from when she found it.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer says that for four kinds of women, their tumah starts only from when they find it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
four women, their time is enough:
a young girl, a woman expecting a baby,

words.note: A girl who never yet became tamei this way.

chunks.en: a woman nursing a baby, and an old woman.
Rabbi Yehoshua said,
"I only heard this about the young girl."
But the halacha is like Rabbi Eliezer.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains who counts as the young girl, the woman expecting, and the nursing woman for this rule.

chunks.en: Who is the "young girl"?
Anyone who never found this sign in her life,
even if she is married.
A woman expecting a baby: from when it is known that she is expecting.
A nursing woman: until she stops nursing her son.
If she gave her son to another woman to nurse,
or she stopped nursing him, or he died,
Rabbi Meir says,
she makes things tamei for a full day back.
But the Sages say,
her time is enough.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains who counts as an "old woman" for this rule, and brings other opinions about women who went a long time without becoming tamei.

chunks.en: Who is an "old woman"?
Anyone who went three
times without it, near the time she got old.

words.note: Each "time" is about a month.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,

chunks.he: כָּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלשׁ עוֹנוֹת,
chunks.en: any woman who went three times without it,
her time is enough.
Rabbi Yossi says,

chunks.he: מְעֻבֶּרֶת וּמֵנִיקָה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עֲלֵיהֶן שָׁלשׁ עוֹנוֹת,
chunks.en: a woman expecting or nursing who went three times without it,
their time is enough.

mishnayos.summary: The rule "her time is enough" is only for the first time she finds she is tamei. The second time, she counts a full day back, unless the first time came from something outside.

chunks.en: When did they say "her time is enough"?
chunks.st: And in the above cases, with regard to what did the tanna say her time is sufficient?

chunks.en: The first time she finds it.
chunks.st: It is with regard to the first sighting

chunks.en: But the second time,
chunks.st: of blood, but with regard to the second sighting,

chunks.en: she makes things tamei for a full day back.
chunks.st: her status is like that of any other woman, and she transmits impurity for a twenty-four-hour period

chunks.en: And if the first time came from something outside her control,
chunks.st: or from her most recent examination. And if she saw the first

chunks.en: then even the second time, her time is enough.
chunks.st: sighting as a result of unnatural circumstances, even with regard to the second sighting, the halakha is that her time is sufficient.

mishnayos.summary: Even with the rule "her time is enough," a woman still needs to check herself at certain times. Kohanim's wives who eat terumah must check even more.

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ,
chunks.en: Even though they said "her time is enough,"
she still needs to check herself,
except a niddah and a woman sitting
in her tahor days after having a baby.

words.note: Days after having a baby when she stays tahor.

chunks.en: And she checks with cloths,
except one in her tahor days after a baby,
and a young bride who is still tahor.
And she needs to check two times:
in the morning and at dusk,

chunks.he: וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁהִיא עוֹבֶרֶת לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת בֵּיתָהּ.
chunks.en: and also when she is about to be with her husband.
Kohanim's wives must do more than them:
when they eat terumah.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
also when they finish eating terumah.

mishnayos.summary: Checking often is praised for women. Women who cannot check for themselves can be helped by others. It also tells how careful Jewish women are to check.

chunks.he: כָּל הַיָּד הַמַּרְבָּה לִבְדֹּק בְּנָשִׁים, מְשֻׁבַּחַת.
chunks.en: Any hand that checks a lot is praised for women.
But for men, it should be cut off.
chunks.explain: For men it is not a good thing.

chunks.en: A woman who cannot hear or speak, a woman who cannot think clearly, a blind woman, and a woman who lost her mind,

words.en: and the woman who cannot think clearly

chunks.en: if they have women with clear minds,
those women get them ready, and they may eat terumah.
The way of Jewish women
is to use two checking cloths,
one for him and one for her.
The very modest ones get a third one ready,
to get the house ready.
chunks.explain: To check before, so that she can be sure she is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: If a sign of tumah is found on the checking cloth, this mishnah tells when the husband and wife are tamei and must bring a korban, and when it is only a doubt.

chunks.en: If it was found on his cloth,
they are tamei and must bring a korban.
If it was found on hers right away,
they are tamei and must bring a korban.
If it was found on hers after some time,
they are tamei because of the doubt, and do not bring a korban.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains what "after some time" means, and how far back her tumah reaches. Rabbi Akiva and the Sages argue whether her husband also becomes tamei.

chunks.en: What is "after some time"?

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרֵד מִן הַמִּטָּה וְתָדִיחַ פָּנֶיהָ.
chunks.en: Long enough for her to get down from the bed and wash her face.
And after that,
she makes things tamei for a full day back, but she does not
make her husband tamei.
Rabbi Akiva says,
she even makes her husband tamei.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּרוֹאָה כֶתֶם,
chunks.en: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Akiva about a woman who finds a stain,
that she makes her husband tamei.

mishnayos.summary: A husband may assume his wife is tahor, even when he comes home from a trip. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue how much checking is needed.

chunks.en: All women are assumed to be tahor for their husbands.
Men who come back from a trip,
their wives are assumed to be tahor for them.
Beis Shammai say,
she needs two checking cloths for
each and every time,
or she must check by the light of a lamp.
Beis Hillel say,
two checking cloths are enough for the whole night.

mishnayos.summary: The Sages used a picture of a house with an inner room, a hallway and an upper room, to explain when a sign that is found makes a woman tamei.

chunks.en: The Sages gave a comparison about a woman:
the room, the hallway and the upper room.
Blood from the room
is tamei. If it was found in the hallway,
if there is a doubt, it is tamei,
because we assume it came from the source.

words.note: The inner room.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the five colors that are tamei, and other colors that the Tannaim argue about.

chunks.en: Five kinds of blood are tamei for a woman:
red, and black,
and like the bright color of saffron,
and like water mixed with earth,
and like mixed wine.
Beis Shammai say,

chunks.he: אַף כְּמֵימֵי תִלְתָּן וּכְמֵימֵי בָשָׂר צָלִי.
chunks.en: also like water of fenugreek, and like the juice of roasted meat.

words.note: A plant with yellow seeds.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say these are tahor.
Green: Akavya ben Mahalalel says it is tamei,
and the Sages say it is tahor.
Rabbi Meir said,
even if it does not make tamei as a stain,
it makes tamei as a liquid.
Rabbi Yossi says,
not this way and not that way.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains each of the five colors that are tamei, comparing each one to something we can see.

chunks.en: What is "red"?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: What is the red

chunks.en: Like the blood of a cut.
chunks.st: color that is impure? It is as red as the blood that flows from a wound.

chunks.en: Black: like ink powder.
chunks.st: What is the black color that is impure? It is blood as black as ḥeret.

words.note: Dark powder used to make ink.

chunks.en: Darker than that
chunks.st: If the black is deeper than that,

chunks.en: is tamei. Lighter than that
chunks.st: the blood is ritually impure; if the black is lighter than that,

chunks.en: is tahor. And like the shine of saffron:
chunks.st: the blood is ritually pure. And what is the color that is like the bright

chunks.en: like its clearest part.
chunks.st: color of the crocus flower that is impure? It is like the brightest part in

chunks.en: And like water mixed with earth:
chunks.st: the flower, which is harvested to produce the orange-colored spice saffron. And what is the color that is like water that inundates red earth

chunks.en: from the valley of Beis Kerem,
chunks.st: that is impure? It is specifically earth from the Beit Kerem Valley and

chunks.en: with water floating over it.
chunks.st: specifically when one inundates

chunks.he: וּכְמָזוּג, שְׁנֵי חֲלָקִים מַיִם וְאֶחָד יַיִן,
chunks.en: And like mixed wine: two parts water and one part wine,
chunks.st: the earth with enough water until it pools on the surface. And what is the color that is like diluted wine that is impure? It is specifically when the dilution consists of two parts water and one part wine,

chunks.en: from the wine of the Sharon.
chunks.st: and specifically when it is from the wine of the Sharon region in Eretz Yisrael.

words.note: A place known for its wine.

mishnayos.summary: When a woman loses a pregnancy very early and only a small piece comes out, is she tamei? The Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Yehudah argue.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a piece,
chunks.explain: A woman who lost a pregnancy very early.

chunks.en: if there is blood with it,
she is tamei.
And if not,
she is tahor.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
either way, she is tamei.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah talks about things that come out of a woman that do not look like a baby, and how we decide if she is tamei and which days she must keep.

chunks.en: A woman who lost something like a peel,
like a hair,
like dust,
like red gnats,
should put it into water.
If they melted away,
she is tamei.
And if not,
she is tahor.
A woman who lost something shaped like fish,
grasshoppers, creeping things or crawling things,
if there is blood with them,
she is tamei.
And if not,
she is tahor.
A woman who lost something shaped like an animal,
a wild animal or a bird,
whether it is a kind that is not kosher or kosher,
if it is a boy,
she keeps the days for a boy.
chunks.explain: The Torah gives different days after a boy and after a girl.

chunks.en: And if it is a girl,
she keeps the days for a girl.
And if we do not know,
she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
But the Sages say,
anything that does not have a human shape
is not a baby.

mishnayos.summary: If what came out was only a sac full of water or other things, it is not a baby. But if it had some shape, she keeps the days for a boy and a girl.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a sac full of water,
full of blood,
full of colored things,
does not need to worry that it was a baby.
But if it had a shape,
she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches about other things that come out with a baby, and why a house where they are found becomes tamei.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a flat shape, or an afterbirth,

words.note: Shaped like the bottom of a shoe.
What holds the baby before birth.

chunks.en: she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
If an afterbirth is in the house,
the house is tamei.
Not because the afterbirth is a baby,
but because there is no afterbirth without a baby.
Rabbi Shimon says,
the baby melted away before it came out.
chunks.explain: So the house is not tamei.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what a woman keeps when we cannot tell if the baby was a boy or a girl, and from when a baby counts as born.

chunks.en: A woman who lost a tumtum,

words.note: A baby whose body does not show if it is a boy or a girl.

chunks.en: or an androgynos, keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.

words.note: A baby whose body has signs of both a boy and a girl.

chunks.en: A tumtum and a boy,
an androgynos and a boy,
she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
A tumtum and a girl,
an androgynos and a girl,
she keeps the days for a girl only.
If it came out not whole, or backwards,
once most of it came out,
it counts as born.
If it came out the normal way,
only when most of its head comes out.
And what is most of its head?
When its forehead comes out.

mishnayos.summary: If we do not know what came out, the woman keeps every set of days she might need: for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah.

chunks.en: A woman who lost something and we do not know what it is,
she keeps the days for a boy and for a girl.
If we do not know if it was a baby
or not,
she keeps the days for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches from which day after the pregnancy started something that comes out counts as a baby. Rabbi Yishmael says a boy is formed by day 41 and a girl by day 81; the Sages say both by day 41.

chunks.en: A woman who lost it on the fortieth day
does not need to worry that it was a baby.
On the forty-first day,
she keeps the days for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah.
Rabbi Yishmael says,
on day forty-one,
she keeps the days for a boy and for a niddah.
On day eighty-one,
she keeps the days for a boy, for a girl, and for a niddah,
because a boy is finished forming by day forty-one,
and a girl by day eighty-one.
But the Sages say,

chunks.he: אֶחָד בְּרִיַּת הַזָּכָר וְאֶחָד בְּרִיַּת הַנְּקֵבָה,
chunks.en: both the forming of a boy and the forming of a girl,
this one and that one are by day forty-one.

mishnayos.summary: The Kutim were not careful with the laws of niddah, so their girls and their beds are treated as tamei. But since this is only a doubt, some strict rules do not apply.

chunks.en: Girls of the Kutim

words.note: A people who kept only some of the mitzvos.

chunks.en: are treated as niddos from their cradle.
And the Kutim make the lower bedding tamei like the upper,
chunks.explain: Even a blanket under many others becomes tamei, as if he lay right on it.

chunks.en: because they are not careful about niddos,

chunks.he: וְהֵן יוֹשְׁבוֹת עַל כָּל דָּם וָדָם.
chunks.en: and their women keep days for every kind of blood.
chunks.explain: They mix up their counting, so they cannot be trusted.

chunks.he: וְאֵין חַיָּבִין עָלֶיהָ עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ,
chunks.en: But one is not punished for going into the Beis HaMikdash because of her,
and we do not burn terumah because of them,
because their tumah is only a doubt.

mishnayos.summary: Tzedukim girls are treated like Kutim women only if they follow the ways of their fathers. Rabbi Yossi says they are like other Jewish women unless they leave the Jewish way.

chunks.en: Girls of the Tzedukim,
chunks.st: With regard to Sadducee girls,

words.note: A group that did not follow the Oral Torah.

chunks.en: when they follow the ways of their fathers,
chunks.st: when they were accustomed to follow in the ways of their

chunks.en: they are like Kutim women.
chunks.st: Sadducee ancestors their status is like that of Samaritan women, whose halakha was discussed in the previous mishna. If the Sadducee women abandoned

chunks.en: If they left to follow the ways of the Jewish people,
chunks.st: the customs of their ancestors in order to follow in the ways of the Jewish people

chunks.en: they are like a Jewish woman.
chunks.st: their status is like that of a Jewish woman.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yossi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: Their

chunks.en: they are always like Jewish women,
chunks.st: status is always like that of a Jewish woman,

chunks.en: until they leave to follow the ways of their fathers.
chunks.st: until they will abandon the ways of the Jewish people in order to follow in the ways of their Sadducee ancestors.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when blood makes things tamei like a niddah, and when it is only like other liquids, for a non-Jewish woman, a metzora'as, and a woman after having a baby.

chunks.he: דַּם נָכְרִית וְדַם טָהֳרָה שֶׁל מְצֹרַעַת,
chunks.en: The blood of a non-Jewish woman, and the tahor blood of a metzora'as,

words.note: A woman with tzara'as.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is tahor.
And Beis Hillel say,
it is like her spit and her other body liquids.
chunks.explain: It makes things tamei only while it is wet.

chunks.en: The blood of a woman who had a baby and did not go to the mikveh,

words.en: a woman who had a baby

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
it is like her spit and her other body liquids.
And Beis Hillel say,
it makes things tamei wet or dry.
And they agree about a woman who had a baby while she was a zavah,

words.en: about a woman who had a baby

words.note: A woman tamei with a special kind of tumah.

chunks.en: that she makes things tamei wet or dry.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah talks about a woman who has pains for days before having a baby, and when she counts as having her baby while she is a zavah.

chunks.en: A woman having pains before birth is a niddah.

chunks.he: קִשְּׁתָה שְׁלשָׁה יָמִים בְּתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר
chunks.en: If she had pains three days within the eleven
days, and she had rest for a full day, and then had the baby,
she counts as having a baby while a zavah.
These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Yehoshua says,
a night and a day,
like the night of Shabbos and its day.
She rested from the pain,
but not from the blood.

mishnayos.summary: How long before the birth can these pains count? Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehudah, and Rabbi Yossi with Rabbi Shimon each say a different time.

chunks.en: How long can her pains be?
Rabbi Meir says,
even forty or fifty days.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
her month is enough.
Rabbi Yossi and Rabbi Shimon say,
there are no pains for more than two weeks.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who has pains during her tahor days after having a girl stays tahor until the next baby comes out. Rabbi Eliezer disagrees, and he and the Sages argue using a kal vachomer.

chunks.en: A woman having pains within the eighty days after a girl,
all the blood that she sees
is tahor, until the baby comes out.
And Rabbi Eliezer says it is tamei.
They said to Rabbi Eliezer,
if in a case where the Torah was strict with blood at a calm time,
it was easy with blood during pains,
then in a case where it was easy with blood at a calm time,
is it not right that we should be easy with blood during pains?
He said to them,

chunks.he: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן,
chunks.en: what we learn from a kal vachomer can only be as strong as where it came from.

words.en: like what it was learned from

chunks.en: What was the Torah easy about for her?
About the tumah of a zavah,
but she is tamei with the tumah of a niddah.

mishnayos.summary: During the eleven days between her regular times, a woman is assumed to be tahor even if she did not check. But at her regular time, she is assumed to be tamei unless she checks.

chunks.he: כָּל אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה.
chunks.en: All the eleven days, she is assumed to be tahor.
If she just sat and did not check,
by mistake, or because she could not,
or on purpose and did not check,
she is tahor.
If the time of her regular time came and she did not check,
she is tamei.
Rabbi Meir says,

chunks.he: אִם הָיְתָה בְמַחֲבֵא וְהִגִּיעַ שְׁעַת וִסְתָּהּ,
chunks.en: if she was in hiding when her regular time came,
and she did not check,
she is tahor,
because fear pushes the blood away.
But the days of a zav and a zavah,
and a woman who waits a day for a day,
these are assumed to be tamei.

mishnayos.summary: A baby born by an operation does not give the mother the usual days after a birth. A woman becomes tamei even before the blood comes out, but a zav only once it comes out.

chunks.en: A baby born through the side,

words.note: Born by an operation, not the normal way.

chunks.en: we do not keep the days
of tumah and days of tahor for it,
and we do not have to bring a korban for it.
Rabbi Shimon says,
this counts as born.
All women become tamei while it is still inside,

words.note: While it is still inside, before it comes out.

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 15:19):
"Her flow in her flesh shall be blood."
chunks.explain: The words "in her flesh" teach this.

chunks.en: But a zav and one who became tamei in another way
do not become tamei
until their tumah comes outside.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what someone eating terumah should do if he feels he is about to become tamei, and that even a tiny amount makes tamei.

chunks.he: הָיָה אוֹכֵל בַּתְּרוּמָה וְהִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁנִּזְדַּעְזְעוּ אֵבָרָיו,
chunks.en: If he was eating terumah and felt his body shake,
he holds himself still and swallows the terumah.
chunks.explain: He finishes eating quickly before he becomes tamei.

chunks.en: And they make tamei in any amount,
even like a mustard seed, and even less than that.

mishnayos.summary: Even a newborn baby can become tamei in many ways, and in many halachos a one-day-old baby counts as a full person.

chunks.en: A baby girl one day old
can become tamei as a niddah.
Ten days old,
she can become tamei as a zavah.
A baby boy one day old
can become tamei as a zav,
and can become tamei with tzara'as,
and can become tamei from a dead person,
and he ties his brother's widow to yibum,

words.note: When a man marries his brother's widow who had no children.

chunks.en: and he frees her from yibum,
and he lets his mother eat terumah,
chunks.explain: If his father was a Kohen.

chunks.en: and he stops his mother from eating terumah,
chunks.explain: If his father was not a Kohen.

chunks.en: and he inherits and passes on an inheritance.
And whoever kills him is punished.

words.en: and the one who kills him

chunks.en: And to his father and his mother
and all his family, he is like a full-grown groom.
chunks.explain: They sit shivah and mourn for him.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches from what age the halachos of marriage and forbidden relationships begin to apply to a girl.

chunks.en: A girl of three years and one day
can become married in that way.
And if her yavam is with her,

words.note: Her husband's brother, for yibum.

chunks.en: he takes her as his wife.
And one is punished for her as a married woman,
and she makes her husband tamei so that he makes tamei
the lower bedding like the upper.
If she marries a Kohen,
she may eat terumah.
If one of the men who are not allowed was with her,
he makes her not allowed to marry a Kohen.
If one of all
the forbidden relationships said in the Torah was with her,
they are put to death because of her,
and she is free.
Younger than that,
it is like putting a finger in the eye.
chunks.explain: It does not count at all.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches from what age the halachos of yibum, tumah and forbidden relationships begin to apply to a boy.

chunks.en: A boy of nine years and one day
who was with his brother's widow,
takes her as his wife.
But he cannot give a get until he grows up.
And he can become tamei through a niddah,
to make the lower bedding tamei like the upper.
And he can make a woman not allowed to eat terumah, but cannot let her eat it.

chunks.he: וּפוֹסֵל אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: And he makes an animal not allowed on the mizbe'ach,
and it is stoned because of him.
And if he was with one
of all the forbidden relationships said in the Torah,
they are put to death because of him,
and he is free.

mishnayos.summary: Children's nedarim count from a certain age: a girl at twelve and a boy at thirteen. In the year before, we check whether they understand what they promised.

chunks.he: בַּת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: A girl of eleven years and one day,
her nedarim are checked.
chunks.explain: We check if she understands to Whom she promised.

words.note: Promises made to Hashem.

chunks.he: בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: A girl of twelve years and one day,
her nedarim count.
And we check her all through the twelfth year.

chunks.he: בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: A boy of twelve years and one day,
his nedarim are checked.

chunks.he: בֶּן שְׁלשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: A boy of thirteen years and one day,
his nedarim count.
And we check him all through the thirteenth year.
Before this time,
even if they said, "We know
for Whose name we made a neder,
for Whose name we made something holy,"

chunks.he: אֵין נִדְרֵיהֶם נֶדֶר וְאֵין הֶקְדֵּשָׁן הֶקְדֵּשׁ.
chunks.en: their neder is not a neder, and what they made holy is not holy.
After this time,
even if they said, "We do not
know for Whose name we made a neder,
for Whose name we made something holy,"
their neder is a neder, and what they made holy is holy.

mishnayos.summary: The Sages compared a girl growing up to a fig: unripe, getting ripe, and ripe. While she is young, her father has certain rights; once she is fully grown, he no longer does.

chunks.en: The Sages gave a comparison about a woman:
an unripe fig, a ripening fig, and a ripe fig.
An unripe fig: she is still a little girl.
A ripening fig: these are the days of her youth.

words.note: A na'arah, a young girl just growing up.

chunks.en: In both of these,
her father gets what she finds, what she makes
with her hands, and canceling her nedarim.
A ripe fig: once she is fully grown,
her father no longer has rights over her.

mishnayos.summary: The Tannaim give signs of when a girl has become a grown-up.

chunks.en: What are her signs?
Rabbi Yossi HaGlili says,
from when a fold grows below the chest.
Rabbi Akiva says,
from when the chest changes shape.
Ben Azzai says,
from when a spot gets darker.
Rabbi Yossi says,
enough that if one puts his hand on
the spot, it sinks in and is slow to come back.

mishnayos.summary: A grown woman or man who never showed signs of growing up may have a body that cannot have children, which changes the halachos of yibum. Beis Hillel and Beis Shammai argue about the age.

chunks.en: A woman of twenty years who did not
grow two hairs,
chunks.explain: Two hairs are a sign of growing up.

chunks.he: תָּבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁהִיא בַת עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה,
chunks.en: must bring proof that she is twenty years old,
and she is an aylonis,

words.note: A woman whose body cannot have children.

chunks.en: she does not do chalitzah and does not do yibum.

words.note: The ceremony that frees a widow from yibum.

chunks.en: A man of twenty years who did not
grow two hairs,

chunks.he: יָבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁהוּא בֶן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה,
chunks.en: they must bring proof that he is twenty years old,
and he is a saris,

words.note: A man whose body cannot have children.

chunks.en: he does not do chalitzah and does not do yibum.
These are the words of Beis Hillel.
Beis Shammai say,
for both this and that, at eighteen.
Rabbi Eliezer says,
for the man, like the words of Beis Hillel,
and for the woman, like the words of Beis Shammai,
because a woman grows up sooner than a man.

mishnayos.summary: There are two signs of growing up, a lower one and an upper one. This mishnah teaches what happens for yibum when only one of them has appeared.

chunks.en: If the lower sign came before
the upper one came,
she either does chalitzah or does yibum.

chunks.he: בָּא הָעֶלְיוֹן עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָא הַתַּחְתּוֹן,
chunks.en: If the upper came before the lower came,
even though that cannot happen,
Rabbi Meir says,
she does not do chalitzah and does not do yibum.
But the Sages say,
she either does chalitzah or does yibum.
Because they said,
the lower can come before
the upper came,
but the upper cannot come
before the lower came.

mishnayos.summary: Anyone who may judge cases of life and death may also judge money cases, and anyone who may judge may be a witness, but not the other way around.

chunks.en: But there are some who may be witnesses and may not judge.

mishnayos.summary: Once a girl or boy grows two hairs, they are grown-ups and must keep all the mitzvos. The mishnah also teaches about the ben sorer umoreh and about a girl's right to refuse a marriage.

chunks.en: A girl who grew two hairs
either does chalitzah or does yibum,
and must keep all the mitzvos said in the Torah.
And so a boy who grew two hairs
must keep all the mitzvos said in the Torah.
And he can become a ben sorer umoreh,

chunks.he: מִשֶּׁיָּבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת עַד שֶׁיַּקִּיף זָקָן,
chunks.en: from when he grows two hairs until a beard grows all around,
the lower one and not the upper,
but the Sages spoke in clean words.
A girl who grew two hairs
can no longer refuse.
chunks.explain: Refuse a marriage her mother or brothers made for her when she was little.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
not until there is more black.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who finds a stain has mixed up her counting. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue whether she must worry about being a zavah.

chunks.en: A woman who sees a stain,
her counting is mixed up,
and she must worry about being a zavah.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
But the Sages say,
stains do not make one a zavah.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who becomes tamei at dusk on a day that is the edge between two kinds of days does not know which day it counts for. Rabbi Yehoshua says to teach the wise women before the foolish ones.

chunks.he: הָרוֹאָה יוֹם אַחַד עָשָׂר בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת,
chunks.en: A woman who sees it at dusk on the eleventh day,

chunks.en: the start of niddah and the end of niddah,
the start of zavah days and the end of zavah days,

chunks.he: יוֹם אַרְבָּעִים לַזָּכָר וְיוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים לַנְּקֵבָה,
chunks.en: day forty for a boy and day eighty for a girl,
at dusk for all of these,
these women are mixed up.
Rabbi Yehoshua said,
before you fix the foolish women,
fix the wise women.

mishnayos.summary: Some things make tamei whether they are wet or dry, and others only while wet. If a dry one can be soaked back to how it was, it still makes tamei.

chunks.en: The blood of a niddah and the flesh of a dead person
make tamei when wet and make tamei when dry.
But the flow of a zav, mucus, and spit,
and a sheretz, a neveilah, and another thing that makes tamei,

words.note: A small creeping animal that makes tamei when dead.
An animal that died without shechitah.

chunks.en: make tamei when wet and do not make tamei when dry.

chunks.he: וְאִם יְכוֹלִין לְהִשָּׁרוֹת וְלַחֲזֹר לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהֵן,
chunks.en: But if they can be soaked and go back to how they were,
they make tamei when wet and make tamei when dry.
And how long is their soaking?
In lukewarm water, for a full day.
Rabbi Yossi says,
the flesh of a dead person that is dry and cannot
be soaked and go back to how it was is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: Stains found anywhere are tahor, except near places where women stayed while tamei. The house of tumah of the Kutim makes tamei because they buried there babies who were born too early.

chunks.en: All stains that are found anywhere
are tahor, except those found in the rooms
and around the house of tumah.

chunks.he: בֵּית הַטֻּמְאוֹת שֶׁל כּוּתִים מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל,
chunks.en: The house of tumah of the Kutim makes tamei through a tent,

chunks.en: because they bury there babies who were born too early.

and an animal would drag them away.

mishnayos.summary: The Kutim are believed about things they are careful with, but not about things they are not careful with.

mishnayos.summary: When a woman finds a stain on her body or her clothes, it depends on where it is: if it could have come from her, she is tamei; if not, she is tahor.

chunks.en: A woman who sees a stain on her body
in a place it could have come from her, is tamei.

words.note: The place it could have come from her.

chunks.en: And not across from that place,
she is tahor.
On her heel or on the tip of her big toe,
she is tamei.
On her leg or on her feet,
on the inside, she is tamei.
On the outside, she is tahor.
And on the sides, on this side or that side,
she is tahor.
If she saw it on her shirt,
from the belt and down,
she is tamei.
From the belt and up,
she is tahor.

chunks.he: רָאֲתָה עַל בֵּית יָד שֶׁל חָלוּק,
chunks.en: If she saw it on the sleeve of the shirt,
if it reaches across from that place,
she is tamei.
And if not,
she is tahor.
If she used to take it off and cover herself with it at night,
any place where a stain is found on it,
she is tamei, because it moves around.
And the same with a head scarf.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who finds a stain may blame it on something else that could have caused it, and then she is tahor.

chunks.he: וְתוֹלָה בְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁהִיא יְכוֹלָה לִתְלוֹת.
chunks.en: And she may blame it on anything she can blame it on.
If she shechted an animal,
a wild animal or a bird,
or worked with stains, or sat
next to people working with them,
or killed a bug,
she may blame it on that.
Up to what size may she blame it?
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
up to the size of a split bean,
and even if she did not kill one.
And she may blame it on her son or her husband.
If she has a wound and it
can open up again and bleed,
she may blame it on that.

mishnayos.summary: A checking cloth was left under a pillow and a mark was found on it. Its shape tells us whether it is tamei.

chunks.en: A checking cloth that was put under
the pillow and blood was found on it,
if it is round, it is tahor.
chunks.explain: A round mark probably came from a squashed bug.

chunks.en: If it is long, it is tamei.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Tzadok.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who goes to the bathroom and finds a sign of blood: is she tamei? Rabbi Meir says it depends how she was sitting; Rabbi Yossi says she is tahor either way.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא עוֹשָׂה צְרָכֶיהָ וְרָאֲתָה דָם,
chunks.en: A woman who goes to the bathroom and finds blood,
Rabbi Meir says,
if she is standing,
she is tamei.
And if she is sitting,
she is tahor.
Rabbi Yossi says,
either way, she is tahor.

mishnayos.summary: If a man and a woman both used the same pot and blood is found, Rabbi Yossi says the woman is tahor, and Rabbi Shimon says she is tamei.

chunks.en: A man and a woman who both went into
the pot, and blood was found on the water,
Rabbi Yossi says she is tahor.
And Rabbi Shimon says she is tamei,
because it is not the way of a man to bleed,
but we assume blood comes from the woman.

mishnayos.summary: When a stain is found on a shirt or bench that more than one woman used, all of them are tamei. But if it was something that cannot become tamei, Rabbi Nechemyah says they are tahor.

chunks.en: If she lent her shirt to a non-Jewish woman or to a niddah,
she may blame it on her.
Three women who wore one shirt
or who sat on one bench,
and blood was found on it,
all of them are tamei.
If they sat on a stone bench,
or on the bench of a bathhouse,
Rabbi Nechemyah says they are tahor,
because Rabbi Nechemyah used to say,
anything that cannot become tamei
cannot become tamei through stains.

mishnayos.summary: If blood is found where three women slept and one of them checks and finds she is tamei, the other two are tahor.

chunks.he: שָׁלשׁ נָשִׁים שֶׁהָיוּ יְשֵׁנוֹת בְּמִטָּה אַחַת
chunks.en: Three women who were sleeping in one bed,
and blood was found under one of them,
all of them are tamei.
If one of them checked and found she was tamei,
she is tamei and the two others are tahor,
and they may blame it on each other.
And if they were not of the age to see it,
we treat them as if they were.

mishnayos.summary: Seven cleaning things are rubbed on a mark to see if it is a stain or just dye. If the mark does not come off, it is dye and everything stays tahor.

chunks.en: Seven cleaning things are rubbed on the stain:
spit with no taste,
and water of split beans,
and mei raglayim,

words.note: A strong, sharp liquid used for cleaning.

chunks.en: and neter, and borit,

words.note: A kind of soap mineral.
A kind of soap plant.

chunks.en: kimonya, and ashlag.

words.note: A kind of cleaning earth.
A kind of cleaning powder.

chunks.en: If he dipped it in a mikveh and handled pure things on it,

chunks.he: הֶעֱבִיר עָלָיו שִׁבְעָה סַמָּנִין וְלֹא עָבַר,
chunks.en: then rubbed the seven cleaners on it and it did not come off,
this is dye,
the pure things are tahor,
and he does not need to dip it again.
If it came off or faded,
this is a stain,
and the pure things are tamei,
and he needs to dip it again.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains some of the seven cleaners and how to use them in the right order.

chunks.en: What is spit with no taste?
Anyone who has not tasted anything.
chunks.explain: Spit from the morning, before eating.

chunks.en: Water of split beans:
chewing split beans,
that are naturally split in half.
Mei raglayim:
that became sour.
And one needs to rub three times
for each and every one.
If he used them out of order,
or if he used all seven cleaners at once,
he has done nothing at all.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who has a regular sign before she becomes tamei counts her time only from when she finds it. The mishnah lists such signs and how a regular sign is set.

chunks.en: Any woman who has a regular time,
her time is enough.
And these are the regular signs:
she yawns, or she sneezes,
or she feels something near her stomach,
or low in her belly,
or something flows, or a kind of shivering comes over her,
and other things like these.
And any sign she has set for herself three times,
that is a regular sign.

mishnayos.summary: If a woman usually becomes tamei at the start or end of her signs, what does it mean for the pure things she handled? Rabbi Yossi and Rabbi Yehudah add more rules about days and hours.

chunks.he: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה בִתְחִלַּת הַוְּסָתוֹת,
chunks.en: If she was used to seeing it at the start of her signs,
all the pure things she handled during the signs
are tamei.
At the end of the signs,
all the pure things she handled during the signs
are tahor.
Rabbi Yossi says,
also days and hours
can be regular times.
If she was used to seeing it
at sunrise,

chunks.he: אֵינָהּ אֲסוּרָה אֶלָּא עִם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
chunks.en: she is only forbidden at sunrise.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
the whole day is hers.

mishnayos.summary: A regular time is set only after it happens three times, and it is removed only after it does not happen three times.

chunks.he: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה
chunks.en: If she was used to seeing it on the fifteenth

chunks.he: עָשָׂר וְשִׁנְּתָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה לְיוֹם עֶשְׂרִים,
chunks.en: day, and it changed to the twentieth day,
both days are forbidden.
If it changed twice to the twentieth day,
both days are forbidden.
If it changed three times to the twentieth day,
the fifteenth is now allowed, and she has set
the twentieth day for herself,
because a woman does not set a regular time for herself
until she sets it three times.
And she is not free from a regular time
until it is uprooted from her three times.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehudah and the Tanna Kamma compare young brides to grapevines: just as every vine is different, every woman is different.

chunks.en: Young brides are like grapevines.
There is a vine whose wine is red,
and there is a vine whose wine is black,
and there is a vine whose wine is plenty,
and there is a vine whose wine is little.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
every vine has wine in it.
And one that has no wine in it,

words.en: and one that there is not

chunks.en: that is a dried-up vine.

mishnayos.summary: When a young bride gets married, Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue for how long a sign she finds is treated as tahor, depending on her age.

chunks.he: תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת וְנִסֵּת,
chunks.en: A young girl whose time to see it has not come, who got married,
Beis Shammai say,
we give her four nights.
chunks.explain: During these nights, a sign she finds is treated as tahor.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
until it heals.
If her time to see it has come, and she got married,
Beis Shammai say,
we give her the first night.
And Beis Hillel say,
until after Shabbos,
four nights.
If she already saw it while she was still in her father's house,
Beis Shammai say,
we give her only the mitzvah of the wedding.
And Beis Hillel say,
the whole night.

mishnayos.summary: A niddah who checked on her seventh day: whether she is treated as tahor or tamei depends on what she found when she checked. Rabbi Yehudah and the Sages add more rules.

chunks.en: A niddah who checked herself on the seventh day
in the morning and found she was tahor,
but at dusk did not check to separate,
and some days later she checked and found she was tamei,
she is still assumed to be tahor.
If she checked herself on the seventh day
in the morning and found she was tamei,
and at dusk did not check to separate,
and after some time she checked and found she was tahor,
she is assumed to be tamei,
and she makes things tamei for a full day back, and from checking to checking.
But if she has a regular time,
her time is enough.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
any woman who did not check to separate in tahor
from minchah time and on,
is assumed to be tamei.
But the Sages say,

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ בַשְּׁנִיָּה לְנִדָּתָהּ בָּדְקָה וּמָצְאתָה טְהוֹרָה,
chunks.en: even if on the second day of her niddah she checked and found she was tahor,
and at dusk did not check to separate,
and after some time she checked and found she was tamei,
she is assumed to be tahor.

mishnayos.summary: People who were tamei in special ways still make tamei by carrying after they die. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue whether every woman who dies is treated as a niddah.

chunks.he: הַזָּב וְהַזָּבָה וְהַנִּדָּה וְהַיּוֹלֶדֶת וְהַמְצֹרָע שֶׁמֵּתוּ,
chunks.en: A zav, a zavah, a niddah, a woman after having a baby, and a metzora who died,

words.en: and the woman after having a baby

words.note: A person with tzara'as.

chunks.en: make tamei by carrying until the flesh rots away.
A non-Jew who died
does not make tamei by carrying.
chunks.explain: This kind of tumah; he still makes tamei as a dead person.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
all women die as niddos.
And Beis Hillel say,
she is a niddah only if she died as a niddah.

mishnayos.summary: If blood came out of a woman after she died, the Tannaim argue whether it makes tamei like a stain and like a dead person.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁמֵּתָה וְיָצָא מִמֶּנָּה רְבִיעִית דָּם,
chunks.en: A woman who died and a revi'is of blood came out of her,

words.note: A small measure of liquid.

chunks.en: it makes tamei like a stain,
and it makes tamei through a tent.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
it does not make tamei like a stain,
because it came loose after she died.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּיוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל מַשְׁבֵּר
chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehudah agrees about a woman sitting on the birthing chair
who died and a revi'is of blood came out of her,
that it makes tamei like a stain.
Rabbi Yossi said,
so it does not make tamei through a tent.

mishnayos.summary: At first the Sages were lenient about a woman in her tahor days after having a baby. Later they said she is like someone who touched a tamei person when it comes to kodashim.

chunks.en: At first they used to say,
a woman in her tahor days after having a baby
could pour water for the korban Pesach.
Then they changed and said,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי הִיא כְמַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת לַקָּדָשִׁים,
chunks.en: she is like someone who touched a person tamei from a dead body, for kodashim,

words.note: Holy foods and korbanos.

chunks.en: like the words of Beis Hillel.
Beis Shammai say,
she is even like one tamei from a dead person.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel agree on many things a woman in her tahor days after a baby may do, but argue whether she needs to go to the mikveh at the end.

chunks.en: And they agree that she may eat ma'aser,
and she may separate challah,
and bring the pieces together and give it its name.
And if some of her spit or her tahor blood fell
on a loaf of terumah,
that it is tahor.
Beis Shammai say,
she needs to go to the mikveh at the end.
And Beis Hillel say,
she does not need to go to the mikveh at the end.

mishnayos.summary: A woman who became tamei on the eleventh day and went to the mikveh too early: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about her tumah and whether a korban is needed.

chunks.en: A woman who saw it on the eleventh day,
and went to the mikveh that night and was with her husband,
Beis Shammai say,
they make lying and sitting things tamei,
and they must bring a korban.
And Beis Hillel say,
they do not bring a korban.

chunks.he: טָבְלָה בַיוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו וְשִׁמְּשָׁה אֶת בֵּיתָהּ
chunks.en: If she went to the mikveh the next day and was with
and after that she saw it,
Beis Shammai say,

chunks.he: מְטַמְּאִין מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב וּפְטוּרִים מִן הַקָּרְבָּן.
chunks.en: they make lying and sitting things tamei, and do not bring a korban.
And Beis Hillel say,
this is a person who is too hasty.
And they agree about a woman who saw it within the eleven
days and went to the mikveh that night and was with her husband,
that they make lying and sitting things tamei, and they must bring a korban.
If she went to the mikveh the next day and was with her husband,
this is a bad way to act,
and what they touched and their being together is left in doubt.
